name_note: Escherichia coli_F is one of several GTDB species split out of the classical Escherichia coli, and the genomes placed here carry the NCBI name Escherichia coli.

sentences.text: Escherichia coli is a Gram-negative bacterium described as an opportunistic commensal of the human gut that can shift to pathogenicity.
A narrative review describes a dual role in the human gut, ranging from harmless commensal strains to pathobionts capable of promoting intestinal inflammation.

That review reports evidence that pathotypes such as adherent-invasive and diffusely adherent E. coli contribute to inflammatory bowel disease, while noting uncertainty about whether they initiate disease.
A study evaluating 430 commensal Escherichia coli isolates found that only a subset inhibited a multidrug-resistant E. coli strain, with carbohydrate competition contributing to niche exclusion.
Gut colonization by multidrug-resistant Enterobacterales, which include Escherichia coli, has been reported to pose a risk for subsequent infections.
